terms.gloss: one who plays the tībia, the reed pipe
evidence: Plaut. Stich. 723: age, tībīcen, quandō bibistī, refer ad labeās tībiās
Cic. de Or. 2.338: tībīcen sine tībiīs canere nōn potest (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: From tībia and canō. The piper accompanied the plays, sacrifices, and funerals.

terms.gloss: a woman piper, a flute girl
evidence: Plaut. Aul. 280–281: condūxit coquōs tībīcināsque hāsce apud forum
terms.comment: Hired with the cooks for a wedding or a dinner.

phrases.latin: age, tībīcen, quandō bibistī, refer ad labeās tībiās
phrases.english: come, piper, now that you have had your drink, put the pipes back to your lips

phrases.latin: At nunc tibi dabitur pinguior tībīcina.
phrases.english: But now you’ll be given the plumper flute girl.

sources: Lewis & Short: tibicen · Lewis & Short: tibicina
